raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Enable the weight cache daemon (`--weight-cache-mode`) on the NPU (Ascend)
backend. Today it is CUDA/ROCm-only: zero-copy weight sharing relies on torch's
`_share_cuda_` IPC handle export, which does not exist on Ascend, so NPU fails
loud with an opaque error. This PR unblocks NPU by moving the transport onto a
backend built on **native torch_npu multiprocessing reduction**, and fixes the
platform fingerprint so a daemon/engine pair running on different Ascend
hardware is correctly rejected as a mismatch (Ascend's reported compute
capability is always `(0, 0)` and cannot distinguish NPU devices).

## Modifications

- **`weight_cache/transport.py`** — add `NpuIpcTransportBackend` (`npu_ipc`) that
  serializes each `tensor.data` with `MultiprocessingSerializer` and reuses the
  existing length-prefixed socket framing (same protocol as `torch_ipc`). On NPU
  the underlying reduction is resolved by torch_npu's natively registered
  `reduce_tensor` / `rebuild_npu_tensor`, so the device index is self-describing
  and no `SGLANG_TP_RANK` is required. `choose_daemon_transport_backend()` /
  `get_client_transport_backend()` route to it when `is_npu()`.
- **`weight_cache/daemon.py`** — allow NPU alongside CUDA/ROCm in `load()`;
  early-return from the CUDA-only `expandable_segments` allocator guard on NPU;
  add `_reserved_memory_bytes()` so preloaded-weight accounting maps to
  `torch.npu.memory_reserved` on Ascend (vs `torch.cuda.memory_reserved`).
- **`weight_cache/protocol.py`** — add a `platform_extra` field to `CacheConfig`
  (part of the struct-equality `matches()` check) and populate it in
  `compute_env_stamp()` for NPU with `device_name`, `device_uuid` and
  `torch_npu.__version__`, covering the `(0, 0)` capability blind spot. CUDA
  keeps it empty and continues to rely on `device_capability`.
- **`weight_cache/ipc_loader.py`** — messages/comments expanded from "CUDA IPC /
  GPU" to the general "zero-copy IPC / device memory" wording; no behavior change.

The transfer is zero-copy by design — the client rebuilds tensors pointing into
the daemon's physical NPU HBM — and safe because plain inference never triggers
`monkey_patch_torch_reductions()`, so `rebuild_npu_tensor` keeps its native
behavior. Functional verification (zero-copy + no `SGLANG_TP_RANK`) is covered
separately by a dedicated NPU test in a follow-up test branch; this PR contains
only the runtime/adaptation changes.

## Accuracy Tests

No model forward / kernel code is changed. This affects only how preloaded
weight tensors are transferred (still byte-identical via zero-copy IPC) and how
the daemon↔engine environment fingerprint is validated. Inference outputs are
therefore unchanged by construction; the fingerprint change is validation-only
and turns previously-accepted hardware mismatches into a clean config mismatch.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Loading and inference paths are zero-copy; no extra data copies are introduced.
The only added cost is a negligible `is_npu()` branch in `choose_daemon_transport_backend()`,
run once per process at startup. No throughput regression is expected.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the `https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit` .
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the `https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests` .
- [ ] Update documentation according to `https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations` .
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to `https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy`  and `https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed` .
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style `https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance` .

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the `https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process` .
2. Get approvals from `https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS`  and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with `https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests`  or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+class NpuIpcTransportBackend(WeightCacheTransportBackend):
+    """NPU (Ascend) transport using native torch_npu multiprocessing reduction.
+
+    Shares the same framing as ``TorchIpcTransportBackend`` (serialize the
+    ``tensor.data`` via ``MultiprocessingSerializer`` -> ForkingPickler, ship the
+    bytes over the existing length-prefixed socket protocol, rebuild on the
+    client with the reconstructed function). On NPU the underlying reduction is
+    resolved by torch_npu's natively registered ``reduce_tensor`` /
+    ``rebuild_npu_tensor``.

+    Verified by smoke test ``_verify_npu_native_ipc.py``:
+      * native NPU reduction works WITHOUT ``SGLANG_TP_RANK`` (device index is
+        self-describing), and
+      * it is truly zero-copy (a client-side write of 12345 is observed by the
+        daemon on the same physical HBM).
+
+    This is safe because plain inference startup never calls
+    ``monkey_patch_torch_reductions()`` (only RL / checkpoint / spec paths do),
+    so ``rebuild_npu_tensor`` keeps its native behavior here and is not forced
+    to read ``SGLANG_TP_RANK``.
+    """
+
+    name = NPU_IPC_BACKEND
+
+    def prepare_export(
+        self, state_tensors: Mapping[str, Tuple[torch.Tensor, bool]]
+    ) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]:
+        entries: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
+        for name, (tensor, is_param) in state_tensors.items():
+            entries[name] = {
+                "handle": MultiprocessingSerializer.serialize(
+                    tensor.data, output_str=True
+                ),
+                "shape": list(tensor.shape),
+                "dtype": str(tensor.dtype).replace("torch.", ""),
+                "is_param": is_param,
+                "device": tensor.device.index,
+            }
+        return entries
+
+    def send_fetch_state_response(
+        self,
+        conn: socket.socket,
+        *,
+        config: Dict[str, Any],
+        entries: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]],
+        pid: int,
+        preloaded_weights_bytes: int = 0,
+    ) -> None:
+        send_msg(
+            conn,
+            {
+                "status": "ok",
+                "config": config,
+                "entries": entries,
+                "pid": pid,
+                "transport_backend": self.name,
+                "preloaded_weights_bytes": preloaded_weights_bytes,
+            },
+        )
+
+    def recv_fetch_state_response(
+        self, sock: socket.socket, result: Dict[str, Any]
+    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+        return result
+
+    def import_tensor(self, entry: Dict[str, Any]) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return MultiprocessingSerializer.deserialize(entry["handle"])
+
+

     state_tensors: Mapping[str, Tuple[torch.Tensor, bool]],
 ) -> WeightCacheTransportBackend:
+    from sglang.srt.utils.common import is_npu

         logger.info("[weight_cache] Using transport backend: %s", VMM_FD_BACKEND)
         return VmmFdTransportBackend()
@@ -198,6 +274,8 @@ def choose_daemon_transport_backend(

+    if name == NPU_IPC_BACKEND:
+        return NpuIpcTransportBackend()
     if name in (None, "", TORCH_IPC_BACKEND):
         return TorchIpcTransportBackend()
     if name == VMM_FD_BACKEND:
